events.summary: Doctors investigate the murder through blood splatter. events.title: DEV DIARY 6b: A Look at Police
events.summary: Police investigators specialize in fingerprint evidence. Police profession icon; Police inspecting footprints; full-body front-view of Police.Using their fingerprint kit, Police players can collect fingerprints from other players and compare them against fingerprints found on objects throughout Whitechapel. events.title: DEV DIARY 6a: A Look at News Hawks
events.summary: News Hawks are investigators of information in Whitechapel. News Hawk profession icon; News Hawk taking a camera; full-body front-view of News Hawk.Using their camera, News Haws can take photographs of other players and bring those photos to witnesses throughout the city. Witnesses can then provide information about whether the person in the photograph passed through their area before the murder. events.title: DEV DIARY 6: A Look at the Professions
events.summary: In Whitechapel, everyone has a role to play. When a murder occurs in Ripper Mode, figuring out who is responsible means gathering evidence, comparing information, and working together to separate the truth from the lies. That's where professions come in. At the start of each match, players will be able to choose from one of three professions: News Hawk, Police, or Doctor. events.title: DEV DIARY #5: Death Isn't Forever
events.summary: In Whitechapel, death is rarely the end of the story. One of the biggest challenges while designing 4 Penny Coffins was answering a simple question: "What happens when a player dies?" In many multiplayer games, death means waiting. You spend the rest of the match watching other people have fun while you hope the round ends quickly. We wanted to avoid that entirely. Instead, we designed death to be another part of the investigation. Justice Comes to Whitechapel Every night ends with a difficult d

events.title: DEV DIARY #4: A Look at 4 Penny Coffins' Game Modes
events.summary: One of the questions we hear most often is: "What's the difference between Magistrate Mode and Ripper Mode?"While both modes share the same Victorian world, investigation mechanics, and evidence systems, they're designed to deliver two very different experiences.So, What is the Difference?Magistrate Mode is a replayable investigation campaign for 1-5 players, where you and your team work together to solve procedurally generated cases against an AI-controlled Ripper.Ripper Mode transforms those s

events.title: DEV DIARY #3: Evidence is Everything
events.summary: In most social deduction games, players rely on instinct, behavior, verbal testimony, and social cues to uncover the truth. In 4 Penny Coffins, evidence is key, but it doesn't always mean truth. We wanted players to feel like they were building a case the way a detective would, which meant introducing physical evidence that players could collect, share, and draw conclusions from. At the same time, we wanted to preserve the social element that makes the genre so compelling. Every crime scene leav

events.title: DEV DIARY #2: A Look at the Ripper
events.summary: A Look at the Ripper in 4 Penny Coffins In 4 Penny Coffins, one player takes on the role of the Ripper: a victim of demonic possession that demands bloodshed at any cost. While innocent players investigate crime scenes, compare evidence, and attempt to uncover the truth, the Ripper works in the shadows manipulating suspicion to survive long enough to carry out the demon’s will.
